subject.title: ACP session identity stuck in "pending" state after gateway restart storm, causing messages to be unrouted to bound ACP agent

question: Should ACP restart recovery be fixed by a status/liveness-backed persistent-session re-ensure path while keeping ensure-sourced ids provisional, or should pending identities with stable ids become resolved without runtime confirmation?
rationale: Both paths can address the report, but they encode different persisted-session contracts and upgrade behavior; automation should not choose that compatibility boundary while an overlapping PR is already blocked on session-state risks.

options.title: Status-Backed Recovery
options.body: Keep ensure-created ids provisional, add persistent-session liveness/status recovery that recreates or resumes the runtime safely, and require configured-channel restart proof.

options.title: Resolve Pending Stable IDs
options.body: Treat pending identities with stable ids as resolved immediately, accepting the risk that ensure-sourced ids become authoritative before status or event confirmation.

options.title: Adopt Warm-Restore PR
options.body: Use the open warm-restore PR as the implementation base only after its missing/dead-PID, persistent-only, rebase, and real-proof blockers are repaired.

recommendation.title: Status-Backed Recovery
recommendation.body: Keep ensure-created ids provisional, add persistent-session liveness/status recovery that recreates or resumes the runtime safely, and require configured-channel restart proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current recovery contract lives in the ACP control-plane split and runtime resume-state helpers that recent history ties most directly to this owner.
